title: Add CarPlay support for head-unit build 21.27.4 (variant 7) — probe: proven: no, patchable: yes
body:
### Setup
- Car: BMW X7 (G07, 2021), iDrive 7 / MGU
- mgu-store + idrive-apps installed cleanly, Store online.
- cluster-render connects and works: `connected to the cluster renderer (id7; map:1088x480, panel:1920x720, hud:800x480)`, layers created.

### Problem
Waze/Apple Maps cluster + HUD map stays `waiting for CarPlay (0 B)`. BMW's native turn box still shows, but the custom map/HUD video stream never starts, regardless of active navigation or head-unit reboots.

### Diagnosis (app's carplay-probe)

target: /usr/bin/carplay
version: 21.27.4
build-id: 389c1d0536f8cc9283c156410f2f2634a9f952c0
sha256: fb5d6b179ad4f62a968697d21e84dbb80adc1ad8e618a6f02c6a9a0467aca1ac
proven: no
variant: slot 0x2b8ef0 (table 0x2b8ed4, 12 slots): ORIGINAL (2nd display gated off for variant 7)
sink: slot 0x29bb10 (59 bytes): ORIGINAL (2nd stream -> AVB stream 15)
selfstart: call 0x1802dc in onSuggestUi 0x180260 (setStreamStatus 0x1800d0, requestStream 0x180380): ORIGINAL (waits for NavController; stream never starts)
res: immediates 0x20b462 0x20b484 0x20b496 0x20b4a4 (builder 0x20b460): ORIGINAL (IC_HIGH advertises 1920x900)
patchable: yes


### Pipeline state
- status: `"page":"waiting for CarPlay (0 B)"`, state idle, hide_bmw_guidance 1, cluster 1, hud 1.
- probe: `rtp packets=0`, decoder `waiting for the stream's first SPS (0 frames decoded)`.
- renderer OK; map/hud layers `hidden` only because there is no stream.

### Ask
`patchable: yes` — offsets are located but not applied because 21.27.4 isn't in the proven list, so `variant`/`selfstart` stay ORIGINAL and the 2nd-display stream is gated off for variant 7. Could you verify/add offsets for build 21.27.4 (variant 7)? Happy to provide the full `woc-logs` tarball and the carplay binary hash above.

[woc-logs-20261107T035139Z.tar.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34509972/woc-logs-20261107T035139Z.tar.gz)

title: HUD map (prototype): mindflow-hud 0.6.0, robertn_hud_map 0.6.0
body:
## HUD map (prototype): `mindflow-hud` 0.6.0, `robertn_hud_map` 0.6.0

A clean navigation HUD drawn through `cluster-render`'s HUD target. BMW's own
speed readout, speed limit and assist icons stay visible next to it.

![The HUD map on the road](https://github.com/polyphia/idrive-apps/blob/hud-map/apps/robertn_hud_map/docs/hud-photos.png?raw=true)

*Photos from the driver's seat at night. The photos were heavily denoised.*


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6fa58a4a-5cb2-4a51-b8ae-4a8932183d87


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf8d6595-37d4-4793-89fb-b4f7f7898d25


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fad76b84-9017-4ef1-9498-51e3c0ac606b



**This is a prototype.** It runs on the car it was developed on (iDrive 7 MGU, P18_23w44.2-1-3, Android Auto) and
needs further work before it is a finished app; see Known issues.

### Why

The main motivation was keeping the HUD map very clean and as close to looking native as possible. Overlaying and
masking Google Maps or Waze themselves never got there: it always looked messy and distracting on a HUD. Drawing our
own map from vector road data gives us true transparency and customization . 

I also tried several ways of placing the car and route from the phone's picture, including tracking the position of
the arrow in Google Maps and Waze. None of them produced results as good as having real geometry to draw.

### How it works

Everything comes from interfaces the head unit publishes to apps over SOME/IP. Nothing patches BMW software or reads
another process's memory.

- **Position:** the app subscribes to BMW `Positioning` (`rawPositionData`: fix, heading, UTC time; `currentLocation`:
  BMW's map-matched, dead-reckoned position). Without a satellite fix (garage, tunnel) the map follows
  `currentLocation`, so it shows as soon as the car starts.
- **Map:** the service fetches Mapbox Streets vector tiles around and ahead of the car and draws the roads in
  perspective, turned to the direction of travel, with the current road's name and the streets ahead.
- **Turn guidance:** with Android Auto navigating, `aapd` converts Google Maps' maneuvers into BMW guidance events and
  pushes them into BMW navigation (`ProjectedModeGuiding`). BMW's own HUD reads them from `GuidanceEventList` view
  `HUD.RB.Main`. The app reads the same list read-only (`getViewConfig`, then `queryContent` every 500 ms) and the
  service draws the next maneuver. The HUD map and BMW's HUD guidance share one HUD slot, so while the map is shown,
  turn guidance has to come from us.
- **Renderer:** at most one geometry update per part per second (cluster-render's limit), with an automatic retry if
  a frame is ever refused.

### The challenge: route geometry

What a navigation map really needs is the route geometry, the polyline of the route ahead. Getting it from Android
Auto / `aapd` has been challenging so far. Android Auto projects only maneuvers (turn, distance, lanes, distance and
time to the destination), not the route's coordinates. Even the projected destination arrives with
`coordinatesValid: false`. Reading the route out of `aapd` means instrumenting a closed binary at addresses that
change with every firmware build: it worked in an emulator for one build and broke on the next. That is why this
version uses the car's own position and BMW's own guidance list, both through published interfaces, which survive
firmware updates.

### Predicting the route from next-turn updates

Without the route geometry, the route line is predicted one segment at a time from what Android Auto does give us:
the car's position and heading, and the next maneuver (turn direction, road name and distance to the turn).

1. **One segment per maneuver.** When a new next turn arrives (for example *right onto Street X in 270 m*), the turn
   point is projected ahead of the car along its heading, at the reported distance. A target is placed about 140 m
   past that point, offset in the direction of the turn.
2. **Snap it to real roads.** The segment from the car to that target is requested as a short driving route (Mapbox
   Directions). The result follows the actual streets through the turn, instead of being a straight line.
3. **Hold it steady, then iterate.** The segment is drawn as the route ribbon and kept unchanged while the same
   maneuver is ahead. It is only re-planned when the next maneuver changes (direction or road), or after about 250 m,
   so the line doesn't jump while driving. Each new turn adds the next segment, so the route is rebuilt turn by turn
   as you drive.
4. **Between plans,** or before the first plan arrives, a short line straight ahead along the heading fills in.

This gives a route line that matches Google Maps' route for the next turn, without any access to the route itself.
Its limits:
- the distance to the turn is approximate;
- with several side streets close together the projected point can pick the wrong one;
- roundabouts and complex junctions need extra care;
- only the stretch up to the next turn is known, never the route beyond it.

This prediction was developed and tested in the PC simulator. On the car the route line isn't drawn yet although the logic is already implemented (see Known issues), so bringing this segment prediction to the head unit is the next step.


**A companion app** could be an alternative: an Android app that knows the destination (by starting the trip or by
sharing the place to it) could compute or receive the route and send its geometry to the head unit over Wi-Fi. I
haven't worked on this yet.

### Features

- Road map from Mapbox vector tiles, fading with distance, with street names.
- Car position from BMW positioning, including without GNSS.
- **Speed camera points database:** fixed cameras from OpenStreetMap (regional packs in
  [Vela](https://github.com/PimpinPumpkin/Vela)'s public road-features format, cached on the unit, plus live Overpass
  queries), matched to the direction of travel, with an icon and a warning.
- An iDrive settings page: on/off, zoom, size, position, viewing distance, horizon, road opacity, camera warnings.
- Fully customizable, we can add any element to our navigation hud in the future (police reports, traffic (already built in), mobile speed cameras alerts, android notifications, etc) 

The possibilities are almost limitless: the scene is our own, so anything the car or the phone can tell the head unit
can be drawn on it. Turn indications are an example. The guidance feed and turn panel are already implemented, but
they don't work on the car yet.

### Known issues

- **The route line isn't drawn.** Without route geometry the scene gets a placeholder route, which it leaves out.
  Drawing the route's upcoming streets should be an easy fix.
- **Turn indications** are implemented but not yet working on the car.
- `overpass-api.de` refuses the TLS of the unit's Node 8, so only the regional camera packs work there.
- The map uses one public Mapbox token (`native/mindflow-hud/mapbox.json`). A private `mindflow-hud-routing` tool can
  override it.
- Tested on one car (G-series, iDrive 7 with HUD).

### Files

- `native/mindflow-hud`: the service. Its npm dependencies live in `vendor/` and are installed as `node_modules/` by
  `component.json`, because the repo's `.gitignore` excludes `node_modules/`.
- `apps/robertn_hud_map`: the settings app; its build script is the one from `apps/robertn_waze_cluster`.
- `release/texts/*.json`: titles and descriptions in all 32 languages.
- README rows for both.

`node release/release.js check mindflow-hud robertn_hud_map`: both reproducible. `node release/test/release_test.js`:
9/9 passed.

title: waze-on-cluster: CarPlay cluster map disappears for 3–5 seconds after Siri finishes
body:
## Summary
On a 2021 BMW 530e (G30, iDrive 7 / MGU), the Waze map displayed in the instrument cluster through **Waze on Cluster** disappears for approximately **3–5 seconds immediately after a Siri request/response finishes**, then reappears on its own.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Connect an iPhone through Apple CarPlay and display Waze in the instrument cluster using Waze on Cluster.
2. Invoke Siri and complete a voice request, allowing Siri to finish its response.
3. Observe the cluster map immediately after Siri finishes.

## Actual behavior
The map briefly disappears for about 3–5 seconds after Siri has completed the interaction, then returns automatically without reconnecting the phone or restarting the head unit.

## Expected behavior
The map should remain present or recover without a noticeable blank interval after a normal Siri interaction, provided the phone is still supplying a valid map stream.

## Possible area to investigate
The README documents `blank_ms` at 10 s, but a CarPlay cluster-stream connection closing causes the map to be taken down at the next periodic check. The shorter 3–5 s interruption might indicate the CarPlay alternate-display stream temporarily stops/restarts or that the map render/session is relinquished and recreated as Siri's UI exits. This is **only a hypothesis**, not a confirmed cause.

## Environment / follow-up
- Vehicle: **2021 BMW 530e (G30)**
- Head unit: **MGU / iDrive 7**
- Projection: **Apple CarPlay**, displaying **Waze** on cluster
- Exact versions of waze-on-cluster, cluster-render, iOS, Waze, and MGU firmware: **not captured yet**
- Not yet checked whether this also occurs with Apple Maps/Google Maps or whether the center iDrive CarPlay map stays continuously visible.

I can provide a diagnostic capture/logs around a Siri request and exact versions if useful.

title: HUD map stays on “Starting” on BMW F44 218i: slot 0x323 locked while cluster map works
body:
# HUD map stays on “Starting” on BMW F44 218i: slot 0x323 locked while cluster map works

## Vehicle and setup

- BMW 218i Gran Coupé, chassis F44
- iDrive 7 / MGU
- cluster-render: 0.4.1
- waze-on-cluster: 0.9.1
- The HUD displays the normal BMW speed information correctly.

## Problem

The map displays correctly on the instrument cluster, but the HUD map remains on “Starting” when HUD display is enabled.

The cluster renderer status reports that the HUD target is waiting for a locked slot:

```text
target map: slot 0x100 scene 0x10004f0 1088x480: shown (us)
target hud: slot 0x323 scene 0x1000400 800x480: waiting slot locked
```

The HUD video layer has sent no frames, while the map layer on the instrument cluster is shown:

```text
layer 3 video of waze-on-cluster on hud:
  waiting - target waiting: slot locked
  0 sent

layer 4 video of waze-on-cluster on map:
  shown
```

At the time of the log capture, Waze was shown on the cluster at approximately 29 frames per second, while `hud_state` remained `starting`.

## Possibly related

This looks similar to issue #85, where an F40 HUD used different display slots from the one selected by default:

https://github.com/robertnisipeanu/idrive-apps/issues/85

However, I have not verified which slots or HUD dimensions are available on this F44, so I cannot confirm that it uses the same configuration as the F40.

## Suggested improvement

Could cluster-render detect the HUD variant and select a compatible display slot and canvas size where supported?

A clearer status message could also help when the configured HUD slot remains locked, for example:

> HUD slot unavailable — this HUD variant may need a different configuration.

For unsupported or unknown variants, a diagnostic showing the available HUD slots would help users collect the information needed for compatibility work.

## Logs

Diagnostic archive captured on 2026-11-06:

`woc-logs-20261106T155427Z.tar.gz`

Please let me know which additional read-only diagnostics would be useful for identifying the HUD variant and available slots.

title: waze-on-cluster: AA cluster map on aapd 21.15.4 (MGU J18_21w19, F40) and HUD map on the F40's smaller HUD (slot 0x351)
body:
Here is another data point for the per-build edit table in #69. On a 2021 F40 with MGU firmware `J18_21w19.2-1-5`, the four Android Auto edits apply unchanged at new offsets, and the Google Maps cluster view now shows in the cluster. I also got the map onto the F40's smaller HUD, which uses different DCSM slots than G05/G80. Both results are confirmed in the car.

### Car and software

- BMW F40 M135i (2021), MGU HIGH F (`hwvariant=HIGHF`), firmware `J18_21w19.2-1-5`, `KI_KOMBI_VARIANT` 7, 10.25" cluster, HUD.
- waze-on-cluster 0.9.0, cluster-render 0.4.0 and robertn_waze_cluster 0.6.0 from the catalog.
- The install hook reported `aapd left as it is: untested aapd build` and `carplay left as it is: untested carplay build`.

## 1. Android Auto cluster map: aapd 21.15.4

| | |
|---|---|
| package | `aapd 21.15.4+gitrAUTOINC+2dcf4a46bc-r0` |
| file | `/usr/bin/aapd`, 7 331 096 bytes |
| sha256 | `f2b2bc5dc395a39c983a7ce8906390c4aa934901d515d6a809322669428bd690` |
| build-id | `1da0c5d951fb82f41e0c5183520b0d727815b62d` |
| aapd.conf sha256 | `9584c540f287bb79744e79cf973795208719ca798f13d881c4dac582656b0f16`, the same as the proven original |

The binary already names `avb://media_transport.avb_streaming.15?mime_type=video/H264` as the secondary display's sink.

The stock and patched bytes are the same as for 22.39.3. Three sites move by -0xe70 and the gate by -0xb70. Every before-anchor is unchanged. The after-anchors of the guard and the screen edit differ, because each contains a rel32 or RIP displacement. Each before + stock + after sequence occurs exactly once in the file.

```js
var KNOWN = { version: 'aapd 21.15.4+gitrAUTOINC+2dcf4a46bc-r0', size: 7331096,
    sha256: 'f2b2bc5dc395a39c983a7ce8906390c4aa934901d515d6a809322669428bd690' };
var EDITS = [
    { name: 'gate', off: 0x98d4d, original: '83bb1c02000001', patched: '83bb1c02000002',
      before: 'ff928000000084c0740a', after: '0f96c0488b4c240864' },
    { name: 'selfstart call', off: 0x1d357b, original: 'e800f8ffff', patched: 'e840fbffff',
      before: '4889442410', after: '488b442428' },
    { name: 'selfstart guard', off: 0x1d30ed, original: '0f848d000000', patched: 'e98e00000090',
      before: '837b4402', after: 'e83809ebff' },
    { name: 'screen', off: 0x15a5d0, original: '660fefc0ebe1662e0f1f840000000000', patched: '83f802740b660fefc0ebdc0f1f440000',
      before: '4883c418c30f1f4000', after: 'f20f1005a8493c00ebcd' },
];
```

I checked each site with objdump:

- **gate (0x98d4d):** The function at 0x98d20 (called from 0x9c5f4) is `call [rdx+0x80]; test al,al; je; cmp dword [rbx+0x21c],1; setbe al`. It is the same field as in 22.39.3.
- **selfstart call (0x1d357b):** This is in `AlternateDisplays::onNewNavigationStatus`, whose `__PRETTY_FUNCTION__` at 0x53a3c0 is loaded there, right after the "Send unavailable stream status to nav" log. Stock calls 0x1d2d80. Patched calls 0x1d30c0.
- **selfstart guard (0x1d30ed):** 0x1d30c0 is `AlternateDisplays::requestStream()`, which loads its name at 0x53a440. `cmp [rbx+0x38],2` stays. `cmp [rbx+0x44],2; je 0x1d3180` becomes `jmp 0x1d3180; nop`.
- **screen (0x15a5d0):** The helper at 0x15a590 returns 12.3 (0x51ef90) for class 0, 10.25 (0x51ef98) for class 1, and otherwise runs `pxor`. Patched, `cmp eax,2; je 0x15a5e0` reaches the 12.3 load.

The patched file differs in 21 bytes. Its sha256 is `259e1278503de73e68ee465734cb378c74d5a170986d17677d5ae77f4911c111`.

**On the car:**

1. I replaced `KNOWN`/`EDITS` in the installed `aapd_patch.js` with this profile. This is a single build, not the #69 table.
2. I restarted the head unit, then sent `{"cmd":"aa-apply"}` to patchd. patchd reported `patched OK` with the sha256 above and restarted aapd.
3. The capture log showed `sequence 1280x720`, the map going to 1088x480, and `render: map shown`.
4. During an active route, the Google Maps map shows in the cluster's map area.
5. The touchscreen and the iDrive controller still work in Android Auto, so the input problem from the #69 incident did not appear.
6. The patch survived several head-unit restarts. Boot recovery reports `aapd healthy` with 0 crashes.

Not tested yet: Waze over Android Auto, sleep/wake, longer drives, and CarPlay (no iPhone). For reference, CarPlay on this firmware: `/usr/bin/carplay` is 3 443 960 bytes, sha256 `5b261f503b6a7a0e4c5610569d2977e731838f9f1aa5824bbcdd060938ffb073`. It is left unpatched.

## 2. HUD map on the F40's smaller HUD

With `hud = 1`, cluster-render reported `target hud: slot 0x323 ... waiting slot locked`. The F40 HUD uses a different slot set.

**Slot table on this car**, from the cluster-render log:

| slots | status | content |
|---|---|---|
| 0x300–0x302, 0x311, 0x321–0x323, 0x330–0x332, 0x361 | 0 (disabled) | none |
| 0x350 | 1/2 | BMW's HUD guidance `0x1000210` |
| 0x351, 0x352 | 1 | empty |
| 0x371, 0x373 | 1 | empty |
| 0x372 | 1/2 | `0x1000251` class 512 for ~10 s (HUD pop-up, like 0x322 on G05) |

**HUD size:** `/mnt/dataro/data/hmi/common/widget/constregistry.pbconst` has two HUD variants. `hudh*` is `hudhWidth` 328 and `hudhListHeight`/`PopupHeight` 280. `hudm*` is `hudmWidth` 232 and `hudmListHeight`/`PopupHeight` 132. The F40 has the "m" HUD. With `hud_size = 800x480` only the bottom-left corner of the scene was visible.

**What I changed for the test:**

- `hud_rules()` only admits `kHudSlot` 0x323. In the 0.4.0 iDrive 7 binary that is the immediate of `cmp rdx,0x323` at 0x66f6c (`4881fa23030000`). I changed it to 0x373 first and then to 0x351. That is the only use of `kHudSlot`.
- `cluster-render.local.conf`: `hud_slot = 0x351`, `hud_yield_slots = 0x372`, `hud_size = 232x132`.
- `waze-on-cluster.local.conf`: `hud_black_background = 0`. With Google Maps' night cluster view the default blacked out the roads together with the background, and only the white labels (ETA, distance) were left in the HUD.

**Results:**

- **0x373:** The KOMBI accepts it (`E_DCSM_OK`, map 1). It is the HUD's lower-left zone, where the speed and the speed-limit sign are, and both are drawn over the map.
- **0x351:** This works. It is the right-hand navigation zone. The map shows there and BMW's turn arrow, distance and street name are drawn over it. Speed and limit stay clear. At 85 % (197x87) and moved to the corner the map fills that zone.
- **HUD "Navigation" setting:** Unchecking it once locked 0x350–0x352 (status 0) for about 3 s, then they came back. With an active Android Auto route, unchecking it later had no effect on the slot table. So BMW's arrow cannot be hidden while keeping the map in 0x351.

**Suggestion:** pick the HUD slot and size per HUD variant. For example, allow 0x351 with 232x132 when the slot table reports 0x323 disabled and 0x351 enabled, or read `hudmWidth`/`hudmListHeight`. Then F40-type HUDs would work without a binary edit. I can collect logs or run status/probe commands on this car if that helps.

title: Question: draw to the instrument cluster and the HUD at the same time?
body:
**Question: is it possible to draw to the instrument cluster and the HUD at the same time?**

I'm trying to make my own shift lights app for iDrive 7 that draws through cluster-render. It works well on my car on either display, but I can't show it on the HUD and the instrument cluster at the same time, only one or the other.

**Car:** 2024 BMW X3 M40i (G01 LCI), iDrive 7, M-layout cluster, cluster-render 0.3.x from the Store.

**What I see:** with the app set to draw on both the `panel` and the `hud` target, only the HUD shows anything. The cluster stays empty. If I turn the HUD off, the same lights appear on the cluster panel straight away. Each one works fine on its own.

**What I found in the code:** `cluster-render.conf` gives `panel` and `hud` the same scene id (`0x01000400`), and the comment says two targets with one scene id are never up at once. `scene_ids_allowed` only lists `0x010004f0`, `0x01000400` and `0x010004f1`, and the comment says other ids (7702, 7703) made the KOMBI restart the cluster and the HUD. I also tried drawing the cluster part to the `map` target (`0x010004f0`) while the HUD is on. On my M layout nothing shows there.

**Question:** is there any known safe way to have the panel and the HUD up together? For example a second scene id that the KOMBI takes for one of them, or a different target for the HUD. If not, no problem, I'll keep it to one display at a time. If you have an idea to try, I'm happy to test it on my car and report back what happens.

Thanks for the work on this, it's been great to build on.

title: waze-on-cluster: add opt-in aapd 21.44.4 support, tested on G30
body:
Adds an opt-in Android Auto cluster-map profile for `aapd 21.44.4+gitr825+21296a5-r0.24`, as found on a 2019 BMW G30 with MGU / iDrive 7 and I-Step `S15A-22-11-540`. The existing patcher only recognises 22.39.3, leaving this car with turn instructions but no AA map on the cluster.

## Change

- Select a per-build edit table, retaining the existing 22.39.3 offsets and behaviour. The new profile has the same four edits; three sites move by `-0x70`, and two after-anchors change.
- Pin the pristine binary SHA-256, size, surrounding anchors, original configuration and `KI_KOMBI_VARIANT=7`. Preserve the current upstream head-unit gate.
- Keep 21.44.4 experimental: the first write requires `--experimental` or `WOC_AA_EXPERIMENTAL=1`. The app and install hook leave it untouched until manual opt-in. Subsequent configuration changes, removal and boot recovery recognise its trusted backup.
- Preserve the boot-recovery changes from #68 and the current head-unit rules. Record 21.44.4 as patched but unproven, including on a no-op apply, so it retains the one-failure recovery threshold. The existing proven build retains its two-failure threshold.
- Retain the upstream 0.8.8 permission fixes from #52. Test apply, revert and both no-op repairs on 21.44.4 under umasks 022 and 077, checking access for the service and ownership as well as file contents.
- Add regression tests and document the car result and limitations. Merge main's WOC 0.9.0 / HUD update (`daaa3f7`) and bump the tool to 0.9.1, retaining its cluster-render 0.4.0 dependency.

## Vehicle verification

The owner tested the following on the parked G30, with a **visible map and active route, correctly positioned in Map view**:

| Projection | App | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Android Auto | Google Maps | Passed |
| Android Auto | Yandex Maps | Passed |
| CarPlay | Yandex Maps | Passed after reconnecting CarPlay |
| CarPlay | Apple Maps | Passed in a separate follow-up check |
| CarPlay | Google Maps | Passed in a separate follow-up check |

The car ran WOC 0.8.1 with this profile and cluster-render 0.3.8. This PR ports that profile onto current main, preserving the newer head-unit checks; the full new package has not been installed on the car. A normal head-unit restart activated the patched aapd, whose running hash matched the intended file. CarPlay's binary remained unchanged. The owner also confirmed sound and camera/parking display.

**Limits observed:** Assisted Driving View displaced the map/application windows left; Map view worked. On the first switch from AA to CarPlay the cluster stream was blank/frozen, then recovered after reconnecting CarPlay and resuming navigation, without changing files or restarting services. Neither cause is fixed by this PR. Full vehicle sleep/wake and repeated phone switching remain untested. The car already had a separate Yandex CarPlay safe-area fix; that fix is not included here. Waze was not part of this test session.

**Follow-up incident, 2026-11-05:** The owner reported that AA appeared on the central display but neither touchscreen nor iDrive controller input worked in AA, and the cluster map was absent. BMW menus and the Store still accepted input. A Store WOC update **and a head-unit restart** restored input and both maps. The exact installed update version and incident logs have not been collected. The restart's effect cannot be separated from the update, and this PR does not claim to fix or explain that incident.

A separate local reproduction confirmed that the earlier branch inherited the upstream permission bug: under umask 077, apply and revert left aapd at 0700 and its configuration at 0600. The earlier byte-oriented tests did not catch that. The 0.8.8 merge and the new 21.44.4 permission tests address this defect; it is not a reproduction of the owner's input freeze.

## Validation

- `make -C native/waze-on-cluster test` and `test-x86`: passed after the 0.9.0 merge. The app's `test_control.js` (49/49) and `test_page.js` also passed. The normal host run explicitly skips firmware-dependent cases when their input files are absent.
- `aapd_aa2144_test.js` with private copies of the exact 21.44.4 binary, configuration and coding: **94 checks passed on macOS and on Linux x86-64 with Node 8.16.2**, covering apply/reapply, byte-exact rollback, permission/owner preservation, refusal cases, install/removal hooks and three boot-recovery entry-point scenarios with mocked OS commands. The Linux run used umask 077 and an isolated container with networking disabled and read-only source mounts. This is not a full MGU boot or Android Auto phone-session test.
- Negative control: substituting the previously published patcher (`ff2a2c2`) into the new test tree makes the permission tests fail. The corrected patcher and an unchanged control pass. The earlier branch also caught five controls: CALL→JMP, JMP→CALL, removal of the experimental opt-in check, removal of the head-unit refusal, and incorrectly recording the experimental build as proven.
- `node release/release.js check waze-on-cluster` passed: two clean builds of 0.9.1 produced the same 2,152,707-byte package (SHA-256 prefix `6fcf64f8b325`).
- The 22.39.3 edit table and coding constants match upstream. No real 22.39.3 binary was available for a full end-to-end regression run; its build-selection fixtures still run.

No firmware, coding dumps, keys, vehicle identifiers or private logs are included.

title: CarPlay: Yandex Navigator vehicle marker is left of center; Apple Maps and Google Maps appear centered (ID7 J18_21w31.5-1-5)
body:
Hi Robert, thank you for this project. We installed Waze on cluster through mgu-store on a BMW MGU iDrive 7 and confirmed that Yandex Navigator's CarPlay map does appear on the instrument cluster.

There is an app-specific positioning issue: Yandex Navigator places the vehicle arrow noticeably to the left of the center of the visible map area. We observed this both without an active route and with a route displayed. - Store: 0.9.17

- Connection: iPhone / CarPlay
- Exact iOS and Yandex Navigator versions have not yet been recorded.

We have comparison photos of Yandex Navigator, Apple Maps and Google Maps, but they are not attached to this initial report.

Could Yandex be interpreting the advertised cluster safe area differently? Is there a supported way to center its vehicle marker without shifting or cropping the image for other navigation apps? We have not established the cause, so this is a compatibility report rather than a confirmed diagnosis.

Please let us know which logs or additional details would be most useful.

title: cluster-render 0.3.8: a scene the display removed is asked for again after 250 ms, and probed every 500 ms while the KOMBI is not ready
body:
On my car (iDrive 7) the map on the cluster drops out for a few seconds whenever the KOMBI removes our scene. Most of that gap was our own wait, not the KOMBI's:

- After a removal we waited at least 2 s before asking again.
- The KOMBI then refuses every fetch for 1 to 3 s (the stock HMI's too), once 7 s. On the loaded head unit the refusal alone took 330 ms to come back, so the 300 ms "not ready" window missed it and the retry went to the ladder.

What changed:

1. A removal by the display (slot not locked, nobody else in it, not our release) is asked for again 250 ms after the removal. From the third removal within 30 s shown, it's back on the ladder (no sooner than 250 ms), so a display that keeps dropping the scene isn't hammered.
2. "Not ready" is a fetch that fails within 1 s (was 300 ms) of a request made within 10 s of the removal. It's asked again after 500 ms, up to 8 times (was 1.5 s, 4 times), then the ladder.
3. While a target probes like this, the KOMBI fetching anyone else's content (Dcsm2 reports every content's fetch status) means it accepts fetches again, so the probe goes at once (`SlotManager::on_display_fetched`).

The lock handling from 0.3.5 is unchanged: a locked slot is still not asked for, and a removal with the slot locked doesn't take this path.

Tests
- `make test-x86` (the unit's gcc 7.5 in Docker): all pass. `slots_test` has new cases for the 250 ms retry, the ladder from the third removal, the 1 s / 500 ms x 8 probe, and the pull-forward on someone else's fetch. `dcsm2_port_test` checks that a fetch of content that isn't ours reaches the slot manager.
- One existing case ("a removal, then a lock before its wait is over") now locks 100 ms after the removal, since the wait is 250 ms instead of 2 s.
- Host `make test` doesn't build for me on macOS (`generation_test.cpp`: `mkdtemp` undeclared, a file this PR doesn't touch), so I didn't run `test-js`.
- The same change (on top of 0.3.3) has been installed on my car since November 2. I haven't yet checked on a drive that the map comes back within about a second after a removal.

Update order: cluster-render only, no `requires`.

title: Feed HUD data same as AppleMaps/GoogleMaps
body:
Own car, MGU / iDrive 7. Thanks for waze-on-cluster / cluster-render. This
is about native HUD guidance for Waze, building on what your own docs
already verify. Please correct anything below.

## What your docs already establish (cluster-render README)

- Render targets are `map` (slot 0x100, scene 0x010004f0, 1088x480, central
  map under the gauges), `panel` (slot 0x203, 1920x720) and `hud` (slot
  0x323, 800x480), drawn through the one RAMSES participant / Dcsm2 client
  (iDrive 7) running as hmi_5000.
- The **CarPlay maneuver panel** — "BMW's own CarPlay turn-by-turn box on the
  cluster" — is stock-HMI content **0x01000310**, mapped into slot **0x105**
  (0x103 on some units), class 0, VERIFIED on the car. `guide_hold` hides it
  by mapping an empty scene (0x010004f1) into 0x105 while the video `map`
  shows.
- During that hold you note (VERIFIED 2026-11-03): the box is hidden, **"the
  HUD keeps its guidance, and the box is back after the release. The HUD's
  slots are not touched."**

## The point: the guidance data is already readable on the car

That cluster maneuver panel (0x105 / content 0x01000310) is populated from
the phone's **CarPlay navigation metadata** during a Waze route — that's why
your tool has to hide it. So the structured guidance (maneuver type,
distance, street name) is already crossing CarPlay -> stock HMI and being
rendered natively on the cluster **for Waze**, not just Apple Maps. It is not
stuck in the phone and not limited to the video stream.

Independent static RE of the Waze 5.22.0 iOS binary corroborates Waze emits
this metadata (links WZCarPlayMapController + CPManeuver / CPTravelEstimates /
CPTrip, drives CPNavigationSession: startNavigationSessionForTrip: /
setUpcomingManeuvers: / updateTravelEstimates:...):
  https://github.com/ysiduc/waze   (REA + Ghidra; analysis only, no binary)

## The gap and the question

The **HUD** turn widget is the one place Waze never appears (reported across
BMWs), even though it is also a stock-HMI element fed from the same CarPlay
guidance channel that already fills 0x105. Since the data demonstrably
reaches the HMI for the cluster panel:

1. Where does the HUD turn widget get its guidance — the same CarPlay
   guidance content the 0x105 panel consumes, or a separate KOMBI source?
2. If the HUD is gated to Apple Maps by nav-app identity, is that gate in the
   `/usr/bin/carplay` binary (patchable, like your KI_KOMBI_VARIANT / cluster
   -display ungate) or deeper in the KOMBI HMI?
3. Could the guidance content that already fills 0x105 be routed/duplicated
   to the HUD's guidance slot — i.e. feed the HUD "just like Apple Maps" —
   as a metadata path, with no video to the HUD at all?

If the HUD draws from the same guidance the cluster panel already shows, then
native Waze HUD arrows on ID7 might be reachable without touching the video
pipeline. Happy to capture logs / test patches once my ENET cable is sorted.

Environment: MGU / iDrive 7; carplay build ~22.28.3 (your patch target);
waze-on-cluster 0.8.0; cluster-render 0.3.7. (Waze also needs server-side
flag 1006 for the alternate display, per your README.)

References:
- Waze 5.22.0 static RE (REA + Ghidra): https://github.com/ysiduc/waze

title: Feature request: adjustable cluster map size/zoom and HUD display selection
body: Could you add controls to enlarge/reduce the CarPlay map in the instrument cluster, plus an option to display it on the HUD? ## Requested behavior 1. **Adjust the map size in the instrument cluster.** Offer a smaller central-map view and an expanded/full-screen map view, where supported by the vehicle. It would also be useful to have zoom-in/zoom-out controls for the geographic map scale if the CarPlay stream or navigation app allows this. Resizing the display area and changing the map scale are separate capabilities. 2. **Choose the display location from the app.** Add a menu such as **Display location** with these options: - Instrument cluster — central map - Instrument cluster — expanded/full-screen map - HUD / head-up display — project the CarPlay map on vehicles that support it 3. **Make compatibility clear.** Keep HUD output optional, indicate when the vehicle does not support it, and allow switching back to the central-map view. An expanded map should preserve visibility of essential gauges and vehicle warnings. This would make the map easier to read at a preferred size and let drivers choose between the instrument cluster and HUD. ## Related work I noticed that open PR #41 already proposes HUD output, HUD sizing and an app-level display selector. The HUD part of this request is related to that work; adjustable instrument-cluster map presentation and map-scale zoom are additional requests. PR #42 also looks relevant to configuring the map's display rectangle. ## Reference photos These photos illustrate the desired map presentation and display-location menu. **1. Instrument-cluster map alongside the main CarPlay display** **2. Another instrument-cluster map example** **3. Display-location selector** The Chinese menu options translate to **Central instrument-cluster map**, **Full-screen instrument-cluster map**, and **HUD / head-up display**. The accompanying text notes that HUD display requires vehicle support. **4. Entry point in the CarPlay instrument-cluster navigation menu** The highlighted item is **Display location**, alongside **Enable map**, **Disable map**, and **Map logs**.

title: waze-on-cluster: keep the stock map until the phone's stream shows a picture
body:
Fixes #28 (and the same symptom without a route: the cluster map area black for a minute or more after every start).

## What happens

A phone starts its CarPlay cluster stream with blank frames (as `freeze_watch.h` notes, 93 in about 2 s on the car, then a pause), and draws no map for the cluster until one is open with a route. Those frames make the map layer `ready` in cluster-render (`have_`), so the contending layer takes slot 0x100 from the stock map and shows them: the map area goes black. It is not frozen (the blank frames stop after ~2 s, below `freeze_min_fps`), so it stays black until `idle_ms` (60 s) after the last frame, or until a route makes the phone draw a map.

Reported to us by a G-series driver: on every start, the street name shows but the map area stays black for about 1.5-2 minutes before the stock map comes back; #28 describes the same with the map staying black until a route is started.

## Change

`FreezeWatch` already tracks whether the stream has shown a non-blank picture (`pictured_`). The layer is now visible only while the stream is live, not frozen **and pictured**:

- `FreezeWatch::pictured()`, `VideoProducer::pictured()`
- `MapFeed::set_stream(live, frozen, pictured = true)`: hidden until the first picture; the log says `is live, no picture yet (the stock map stays)` and the status reason `no map picture from the phone yet`
- `main.cpp` passes `producer.pictured()`

Until the phone sends a real map the stock map stays; the first non-blank frame shows the CarPlay map as before. Nothing else changes (frozen handling, stall, targets).

## Tests

- `freeze_watch_test`: the car's blank start has no picture; the first non-blank frame pictures it; a new stream starts without one
- `map_feed_test`: live with no picture yet → hidden, idle, slot released, stock map shown, reason given; the first picture → shown with the frames

`make test`, `make test-x86` and `make target` pass (built in a fork's Actions; the target's 20 imports check against the unit's libraries).

Draft until we have confirmed it on a car; I will update this PR with the result.

title: Subject: Full overview: BMW iDrive 7 (MGU) SSH port 22 unreachable – Store & Waze Cluster install
body:
Subject: Full overview: BMW iDrive 7 (MGU) SSH port 22 unreachable – Store & Waze Cluster install

1. Environment & Setup:
- Vehicle: BMW with iDrive 7 (MGU head unit), stock factory firmware, unpatched (Road Map EUROPE Live 2021-10, no pre-installed dev FSC).
- Host machine: macOS running Node.js.
- Connections tested: Vehicle Wi-Fi access point and ENET cable (OBD to RJ45/USB-C adapter).

2. Troubleshooting Steps & Results:
- Offline USB repository:
  Created the offline repository on a USB drive via `node mgu-install.js usb-repo <USB_MOUNT_PATH>`, containing "mgu-store" and "idrive-apps" (with robertn_waze_cluster). After performing an iDrive hard reboot (holding the volume knob for 30 seconds) and updating BMW apps/services, nothing appears because the Store application is not installed on the MGU head unit yet.
- Direct network installation:
  Both over Wi-Fi (IP 172.16.222.97) and via ENET cable (even with the car in Diagnostic Mode via 3 quick presses on Start/Stop), running `node mgu-install.js first-install --host 172.16.222.97` successfully validates package SHA-256 hashes, then immediately fails at the SSH step:
  "installing on 172.16.222.97:22"
  "ssh: connect to host 172.16.222.97 port 22: Operation timed out"
  "mgu-install: ssh: spawnSync ssh EPIPE"
- Network probing:
  Port checks (via netcat on ports 22, 2222, and 13400) consistently return connection timeouts or connection refusals.

3. Root Cause Identified:
The script `mgu-install.js` acts strictly as a deployment package manager; it does not contain a jailbreak exploit. It requires an active SSH daemon with root privileges already listening on the head unit. On post-2021 BMW factory firmware releases, SSH access is completely disabled by default, and unsigned code execution is blocked.

4. Question / Core Issue:
Is a prior root/patch procedure (e.g., using Windows via FeatureInstaller or injecting root/dev FSC certificates) mandatory to start the SSH daemon before this script can run, or is there an alternative bootstrap method available for stock, unpatched units?

title: Feature request: Android Auto Waze map on the iDrive 7 instrument cluster
body:
Hi, thanks for building the Waze-on-cluster support.

Would you consider adding an Android Auto path for the Waze map on iDrive 7 / MGU, alongside the current CarPlay path?

The current implementation appears to patch and capture CarPlay's cluster map stream. Waze's Android Auto help now says cluster navigation is available on supported vehicles, but BMW/iDrive 7 support may depend on the car and software version. Could this project use an Android Auto-provided cluster/map stream on the MGU, or is there a technical limitation that prevents it?

My use case is a 2019 BMW G20 M340i with an Android phone. I can confirm the exact iDrive/head-unit software version and test on the car if that would help.
